questions.text: कल्पना कीजिए कि आप जनवरी में दिल्ली से चंडीगढ़ एक शादी में शामिल होने के लिए, सड़क मार्ग से जा रहे हैं। यात्रा के दौरान आप निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी फ़सल खेतों में प्रमुखता से देखेंगे?
questions.text_english: Imagine you are travelling from Delhi to Chandigarh to attend a wedding, by road in January. Which of the following crops will you notice prominently in the fields during the journey?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Wheat. January falls in the Rabi (winter) crop season. The Delhi–Chandigarh route passes through the Punjab–Haryana plains, which is the wheat bowl of India. Wheat is sown in October–November and stands tall in the fields during January. Paddy and Maize are Kharif crops grown in summer/monsoon, and Jowar is also predominantly a Kharif crop, so none of them would be prominently visible in January.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) गेहूँ है। जनवरी रबी (शीतकालीन) फसल का मौसम है। दिल्ली से चंडीगढ़ का मार्ग पंजाब-हरियाणा के मैदानों से होकर गुजरता है, जो भारत का गेहूँ उत्पादक क्षेत्र है। गेहूँ अक्टूबर-नवंबर में बोया जाता है और जनवरी में खेतों में लहलहाता दिखता है।

questions.text: कृष्णा – गोदावरी मुद्दे में शामिल प्रमुख राज्यों से संबंधित सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Choose the correct option regarding major states involved in the Krishna – Godavari issue:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. The Krishna and Godavari rivers flow through Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh (including Telangana). These states have long-standing disputes over the sharing of river waters for irrigation and drinking purposes. Kerala is not part of this river basin, and Gujarat/Jharkhand are also unrelated to this dispute.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक और आंध्र प्रदेश है। कृष्णा और गोदावरी नदियाँ महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक और आंध्र प्रदेश से होकर बहती हैं और इन राज्यों के बीच जल-बँटवारे को लेकर विवाद है।

questions.text: स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: स्तंभ I (बाँध) — a. हीराकुड, b. गाँधी सागर, c. नागार्जुन सागर, d. मेट्टूर; स्तंभ II (नदी) — i. चम्बल, ii. कृष्णा, iii. कावेरी, iv. महानदी
questions.text_english: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option: Column I (Dam) — a. Hirakud, b. Gandhi Sagar, c. Nagarjuna Sagar, d. Mettur; Column II (River) — i. Chambal, ii. Krishna, iii. Kaveri, iv. Mahanadi
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii. Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi river in Odisha (a-iv). Gandhi Sagar Dam is built on the Chambal river in Madhya Pradesh (b-i). Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on the Krishna river in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana (c-ii). Mettur Dam is built on the Kaveri river in Tamil Nadu (d-iii).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii है। हीराकुड बाँध — महानदी, गाँधी सागर — चम्बल, नागार्जुन सागर — कृष्णा, मेट्टूर — कावेरी।

questions.text: 'सरिस्का बाघ रिज़र्व' निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य में स्थित है?
questions.text_english: 'Sariska Tiger Reserve' is located in which one of the following states?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Rajasthan. Sariska Tiger Reserve is located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan. It was declared a tiger reserve in 1978 under Project Tiger. It is famous for Bengal tigers and is situated in the Aravalli mountain range. The other options — Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra — have different tiger reserves such as Kanha, Dudhwa, and Tadoba respectively.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) राजस्थान है। सरिस्का बाघ रिज़र्व राजस्थान के अलवर जिले में स्थित है। इसे 1978 में प्रोजेक्ट टाइगर के अंतर्गत बाघ अभयारण्य घोषित किया गया था।

questions.text: भारत में वनों के निम्नलिखित वर्गों को क्षेत्रफल की दृष्टि से सबसे अधिक से सबसे कम के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. आरक्षित, II. रक्षित, III. अवर्गीकृत
questions.text_english: Arrange the following categories of forests in India from the largest to the smallest in terms of area and choose the correct option: I. Reserved, II. Protected, III. Unclassed
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) I, II, III. In India, Reserved Forests cover the largest area (about 54% of total forest area), followed by Protected Forests (about 29%), and Unclassed Forests are the smallest category (about 17%). Reserved forests are under the strictest government control, while unclassed forests are found mainly in the northeastern states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) I, II, III है। भारत में आरक्षित वन सबसे अधिक क्षेत्र (लगभग 54%) में हैं, उसके बाद रक्षित वन (लगभग 29%), और अवर्गीकृत वन सबसे कम (लगभग 17%) हैं।

questions.text: मान लीजिए कि आप 15वीं शताब्दी की प्रिंट संस्कृति पर शोध कर रहे हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा आपके शोध का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण लाभ होगा?
questions.text_english: Assume you are doing research on 15th century print culture. Which of the following would be the most significant advantage for your research?

options.C: पाठों को हाथ से कॉपी करने की क्षमता में बढ़ोतरी
options.D: प्रिंट में तेज़ी और सटीकता में वृद्धि

options_english.C: Increase in the ability to copy text by hand
options_english.D: Increased speed and accuracy of print

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Increased speed and accuracy of print. The 15th century saw Gutenberg's invention of the printing press, which revolutionized the production of books by dramatically increasing the speed and accuracy of printing. This made texts available to a far wider audience. Option A is incorrect because manuscripts were still rare; option B is wrong as libraries became more important; option C relates to the pre-print era.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) प्रिंट में तेज़ी और सटीकता में वृद्धि है। 15वीं शताब्दी में गुटेनबर्ग के प्रिंटिंग प्रेस के आविष्कार से पुस्तकों का उत्पादन तीव्र गति से संभव हुआ, जिससे ज्ञान व्यापक जनसमुदाय तक पहुँचा।
questions.chapter: Print Culture and the Modern World

questions.text: 'बुक ऑफ़ मार्वेल्स' के लेखक हैं:
questions.text_english: The author of 'Book of Marvels' is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Marco Polo. Marco Polo was a Venetian traveller who journeyed to China and the East. His famous travelogue is known as 'The Book of Marvels' (or 'The Travels of Marco Polo'), which described the wealth, culture, and geography of Asia. Columbus and Vasco da Gama were explorers but did not write this book; Alfred Crosby was an American historian.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) माकों पोलो है। माकों पोलो वेनिस के यात्री थे जिन्होंने चीन और पूर्वी देशों की यात्रा की और अपने अनुभव 'बुक ऑफ़ मार्वेल्स' में लिखे।
questions.chapter: The Making of a Global World
questions.topic: Trade and Travel in the Pre-modern World

questions.text: उन्नीसवीं सदी तक लोगों के यूरोप से अमेरिका जाने के निम्नलिखित कारणों को पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. गरीबी और भूख, II. गुलामों की खरीद-फरोख्त, III. बीमारियों का बोलबाला, IV. धार्मिक टकराव और दंड
questions.text_english: Read the following reasons of migration of people from Europe to America till the 19th century and choose the correct option: I. Poverty and hunger, II. Slaves for sale, III. Wide spread of diseases, IV. Religious conflicts and persecution

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, III and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Only I, III and IV are correct. Europeans migrated to America primarily due to poverty and hunger (I), widespread diseases that made living conditions in Europe difficult (III), and religious persecution and conflicts (IV). Statement II — 'Slaves for sale' — is incorrect in this context because slaves were brought FROM Africa TO America and the Americas; they were not a reason for European migration. Hence options containing II are incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) केवल I, III और IV है। यूरोपीय लोग गरीबी-भूख, बीमारियों और धार्मिक उत्पीड़न के कारण अमेरिका गए। 'गुलामों की खरीद-फरोख्त' यूरोपीय प्रवास का कारण नहीं थी।
questions.chapter: The Making of a Global World

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा क्षेत्र 1866 में एकीकृत इटली का हिस्सा बना?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following regions became a part of unified Italy in 1866?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Venetia. The unification of Italy took place in stages. Sardinia-Piedmont was already central to the unification movement from the beginning. Venetia (Venice) was annexed into unified Italy in 1866 following the Austro-Prussian War, when Austria was defeated. Sicily was unified earlier (1860) under Garibaldi. The Papal States were the last to be incorporated in 1870.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) वेनेशिया है। वेनेशिया (वेनिस) 1866 में ऑस्ट्रो-प्रशिया युद्ध के बाद एकीकृत इटली का हिस्सा बना जब ऑस्ट्रिया पराजित हुआ।

questions.text: नीचे दो कथन I एवं II दिए गए हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: कथन I: प्रौद्योगिकी में तीव्र उन्नति वैश्वीकरण की प्रक्रिया को उत्प्रेरित करने वाला एक मुख्य कारक है। कथन II: इसने लंबी दूरियों तक वस्तुओं की तीव्रतर आपूर्ति को कम लागत पर संभव किया है।
questions.text_english: Two statements I and II are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option: Statement I: Rapid improvement in technology has been one major factor to stimulate the globalisation process. Statement II: This has made much faster delivery of goods across long distances possible at lower costs.

options.A: कथन I और II दोनों सही हैं और कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: कथन I और II दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: कथन I सही है, परन्तु कथन II गलत है।
options.D: कथन I गलत है, परन्तु कथन II सही है।

options_english.A: Both statements I and II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
options_english.B: Both statements I and II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
options_english.C: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
options_english.D: Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both statements are correct and Statement II correctly explains Statement I. Technological advancements — such as containerisation, faster ships, and improved communication — have indeed been a major driver of globalisation. These improvements directly enabled faster delivery of goods across long distances at lower costs, which is exactly what Statement II describes. Thus, Statement II is a valid and direct explanation of Statement I.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं और कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या करता है। प्रौद्योगिकी में सुधार (जैसे कंटेनराइजेशन, तेज़ जहाज) ने कम लागत पर लंबी दूरियों तक माल पहुँचाना संभव किया, जिससे वैश्वीकरण को बल मिला।

questions.text: भारत के शहरी क्षेत्रों में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा समूह अपनी ऋण की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए अनौपचारिक स्रोतों पर निर्भर है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following groups in urban India depend on informal sources to meet their credit needs?

options.C: दोनों, गरीब और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार
options.D: दोनों, समृद्ध और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार

options_english.C: Both poor households and households with few assets
options_english.D: Both well-off households and households with few assets

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Both poor households and households with few assets. In urban India, both poor families and families with few assets lack collateral and a credit history required by formal financial institutions like banks. As a result, they are forced to rely on informal sources such as moneylenders, relatives, and friends. Well-off households generally have access to formal credit channels.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। शहरी भारत में गरीब परिवार और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार दोनों ही बैंकों की आवश्यकताएं पूरी नहीं कर पाते, इसलिए अनौपचारिक स्रोतों (साहूकार, रिश्तेदार) पर निर्भर रहते हैं।
questions.topic: Formal and Informal Sources of Credit

questions.text: ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में किसानों के लिए सरकारी बैंकों से ऋण लेना कठिन क्यों हो जाता है? निम्नलिखित कारणों को पढ़िए और सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. ऋणाधार का अभाव, II. जटिल प्रक्रिया, III. ऋण की उच्चतर लागत, IV. जागरूकता का अभाव
questions.text_english: Why does it become difficult for farmers in rural areas to take loans from government banks? Read the following reasons and choose the most appropriate option: I. Lack of collateral, II. Complicated procedure, III. Higher cost of borrowing, IV. Lack of awareness

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, II and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, III and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Only I, II and IV are correct. Rural farmers face difficulty in obtaining government bank loans primarily because they lack collateral (I) — formal banks require assets as security. The complicated documentation and procedures (II) are a major deterrent. Lack of awareness (IV) about bank schemes also restricts them. Statement III is incorrect because formal banks actually offer lower interest rates than informal moneylenders, so 'higher cost of borrowing' does not apply to government banks.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) केवल I, II और IV है। ग्रामीण किसानों के पास ऋणाधार नहीं होता (I), बैंकों की प्रक्रिया जटिल होती है (II), और जागरूकता का अभाव होता है (IV)। सरकारी बैंकों में ऋण की लागत अनौपचारिक स्रोतों से कम होती है, इसलिए III गलत है।

questions.text: दिए गए चित्र को देखिए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए: चित्र में किया जाने वाला कार्य अर्थव्यवस्था के किस क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आता है?
questions.text_english: Look at the given picture and answer the question that follows: The work being done in the picture falls under which sector of the economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Secondary. The picture shows workers engaged in manufacturing/processing of garments in a factory, which falls under the Secondary sector of the economy. The secondary sector involves the transformation of raw materials into finished goods through manufacturing and industrial activities. The primary sector involves agriculture/mining, tertiary involves services, and quaternary involves knowledge-based activities.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) द्वितीयक है। चित्र में वस्त्र निर्माण कारखाने में काम करती महिलाएं दिख रही हैं। कच्चे माल को तैयार माल में बदलने की प्रक्रिया द्वितीयक क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आती है।

questions.text: 'X' एक कस्बे में रहता है। वह फूलों की खेती के साथ-साथ पशुपालन भी करता है। 'X' का कार्य अर्थव्यवस्था के किस क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आएगा?
questions.text_english: 'X' lives in a town. He cultivates flowers along with animal husbandry. The work of 'X' will fall under which sector of the economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Primary. Both flower cultivation (agriculture/horticulture) and animal husbandry are activities that involve the direct extraction or use of natural resources. These activities belong to the Primary sector of the economy. The Primary sector includes farming, fishing, forestry, mining, and animal husbandry. The fact that 'X' lives in a town does not change the nature of the economic activity.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) प्राथमिक है। फूलों की खेती (बागवानी) और पशुपालन दोनों ही प्राकृतिक संसाधनों के प्रत्यक्ष उपयोग पर आधारित हैं, इसलिए ये प्राथमिक क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आते हैं।

questions.text: 'विश्व मानव विकास सूचकांक' से संबंधित निम्नलिखित तालिका का अध्ययन कीजिए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए: दिए गए देशों में से, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश 'मानव विकास सूचकांक' में उच्चतम स्थान रखता है? (तालिका: 1. भारत-130, 2. म्यांमार-148, 3. नेपाल-149, 4. पाकिस्तान-150)
questions.text_english: Study the following table related to 'World Human Development Index' and answer the question given below: Amongst the given countries, which one of the following countries has the highest rank in 'Human Development Index'? (Table: 1. India-130, 2. Myanmar-148, 3. Nepal-149, 4. Pakistan-150)
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) India. In the Human Development Index (HDI), a lower rank number indicates a higher position (i.e., rank 1 is the best). Among the four countries listed — India (rank 130), Myanmar (rank 148), Nepal (rank 149), and Pakistan (rank 150) — India has rank 130 which is the lowest number, meaning India is placed highest among these four countries on the HDI.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) भारत है। मानव विकास सूचकांक में कम क्रमांक (रैंक) अधिक अच्छी स्थिति दर्शाता है। दिए गए चारों देशों में भारत का क्रमांक 130 सबसे कम है, अतः भारत इनमें उच्चतम स्थान पर है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से राजनीतिक दल के मुख्य घटक हैं? सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: I. नेता, II. सक्रिय सदस्य, III. समर्थक, IV. दबाव समूह
questions.text_english: Which of the following are the main components of a political party? Choose the correct option: I. Leaders, II. Active members, III. Followers, IV. Pressure groups

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, III and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Only I, II and III are correct. The main components of a political party are its Leaders (who direct the party), Active members (who work for the party), and Followers/Supporters (who vote and support the party). Pressure groups (IV) are separate entities that try to influence government policies but are not a component of a political party. Pressure groups operate independently and may support any party.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) केवल I, II और III है। राजनीतिक दल के मुख्य घटक हैं — नेता, सक्रिय सदस्य, और समर्थक। दबाव समूह राजनीतिक दल का घटक नहीं होते; वे स्वतंत्र रूप से सरकार को प्रभावित करने की कोशिश करते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से सही सुमेलित युग्म का चयन कीजिए: (देश) — (व्यवस्था)
questions.text_english: Choose the correctly matched pair from the following: (Country) — (System)
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Spain — Federal. Spain has a federal system of government where power is shared between the central government and regional (autonomous) communities. Canada has a Federal system (not Unitary), so option A is wrong. Bolivia has a Unitary system (not Federal), so option B is wrong. Australia has a Federal system (not Unitary), so option C is wrong. Spain's decentralized federal structure makes option D correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) स्पेन — संघात्मक है। स्पेन में संघात्मक शासन व्यवस्था है। कनाडा भी संघात्मक है (एकात्मक नहीं), ऑस्ट्रेलिया भी संघात्मक है (एकात्मक नहीं), और बोलीविया एकात्मक है।

questions.text: बेल्जियम ने अपनी बहुसंख्यकवाद की समस्या का समाधान निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रकार की शासन व्यवस्था को सुदृढ़ करके किया?
questions.text_english: Belgium solved its problem of majoritarianism by strengthening which of the following types of government?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Federal. Belgium has a diverse population with Dutch-speaking Flemish, French-speaking Walloons, and a German-speaking minority. To avoid domination by the majority group and to accommodate all communities, Belgium transformed itself from a unitary state into a federal state, distributing powers among central, regional, and community governments. This federal accommodation is considered a successful model for managing diversity.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) संघात्मक है। बेल्जियम में डच, फ्रेंच और जर्मन भाषी समुदाय हैं। बहुसंख्यकवाद की समस्या से निपटने के लिए बेल्जियम ने संघात्मक व्यवस्था को सुदृढ़ किया और सत्ता का विकेंद्रीकरण किया।

questions.text: स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: स्तंभ I (खनिज) — a. लौह अयस्क, b. अभ्रक, c. बॉक्साइट, d. कोयला; स्तंभ II (प्रमुख खानें) — i. गया, ii. सिंगरौली, iii. चंद्रपुर, iv. मैकाल

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. Iron ore (a) is found in Chandrapur (iii) region. Mica (b) is found in Gaya (i) in Bihar, which is known for significant mica deposits. Bauxite (c) is found in the Maikala (iv) hills. Coal (d) is found in Singarauli (ii), which is one of India's major coal-producing regions in Madhya Pradesh/UP border.

questions.text: नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं। ये अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए: अभिकथन (A): खनिज हमारे जीवन के अति अनिवार्य भाग हैं। कारण (R): सभी सजीव वस्तुओं को खनिजों की आवश्यकता होती है।
questions.text_english: Two statements are given below. They are Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option: Assertion (A): Minerals are an indispensable part of our lives. Reason (R): All living things need minerals.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). Assertion (A) is true — minerals are indispensable in modern human life for industry, construction, technology, and health. Reason (R) is also true — all living organisms require minerals for metabolic processes. However, (R) does not correctly explain (A) because the assertion refers to the industrial and economic importance of minerals in human civilization, not merely their biological necessity for living organisms.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। अभिकथन (A) खनिजों के औद्योगिक और सामाजिक महत्व की बात करता है, जबकि कारण (R) जैविक आवश्यकता की बात करता है, जो (A) की सटीक व्याख्या नहीं है।

questions.text: भारत में 1990 के दशक में शुरू की गई उदारीकरण की प्रक्रिया ने किस प्रकार वैश्वीकरण को बढ़ावा दिया? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did the process of liberalisation initiated in India in the 1990s, promote globalisation? Explain.

key_points: Liberalisation removed barriers to foreign trade and investment, allowing free flow of goods and capital.
It opened Indian markets to multinational companies and enabled Indian companies to expand globally, thus promoting globalisation.

questions.solution: The liberalisation process initiated in India in the 1990s promoted globalisation in two major ways. First, it removed trade barriers such as import restrictions, high tariffs, and licensing requirements, allowing the free flow of goods, services, and capital between India and the rest of the world. Second, it opened Indian markets to foreign investment by multinational companies (MNCs) and also enabled Indian companies to invest and expand in foreign markets. This integration of the Indian economy with the global economy accelerated the process of globalisation significantly.
questions.solution_hindi: 1990 के दशक में शुरू की गई उदारीकरण की प्रक्रिया ने वैश्वीकरण को दो प्रमुख तरीकों से बढ़ावा दिया। पहला, इसने आयात प्रतिबंध, उच्च शुल्क और लाइसेंसिंग जैसी व्यापार बाधाओं को हटाया, जिससे वस्तुओं, सेवाओं और पूंजी का स्वतंत्र प्रवाह संभव हुआ। दूसरा, इसने बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियों के लिए भारतीय बाजार खोला और भारतीय कंपनियों को विदेशी बाजारों में विस्तार का अवसर दिया।

questions.text: भू-निम्नीकरण की समस्या के समाधान के किन्हीं दो उपायों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two measures to solve the problem of land degradation.

key_points: Afforestation and shelter belts reduce wind/water erosion and restore soil fertility.
Proper management of wastelands, reducing overgrazing, and controlling mining activities restore degraded land.

questions.solution: Two important measures to solve the problem of land degradation are as follows. First, afforestation and planting of shelter belts of trees help in controlling soil erosion caused by wind and water. Trees bind the soil and prevent it from being washed or blown away, thereby restoring land fertility over time. Second, controlled and regulated mining, along with proper reclamation of mining areas after use, prevents the dumping of waste and the chemical contamination of soil. Reducing overgrazing by livestock also helps in recovering degraded land.
questions.solution_hindi: भू-निम्नीकरण की समस्या के दो प्रमुख उपाय हैं। पहला, वनारोपण और वृक्षारोपण से वायु और जल अपरदन को नियंत्रित किया जा सकता है। पेड़ मिट्टी को बाँधते हैं और भूमि की उर्वरता बनाए रखते हैं। दूसरा, खनन कार्यों का उचित नियमन और खनन क्षेत्रों का पुनरुद्धार (reclamation) भू-निम्नीकरण को रोकने में सहायक है।

questions.text: भारत की विधायिकाओं में महिलाओं के प्रतिनिधित्व को बढ़ाने के लिए कोई दो उपाय सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any two measures to increase the number of women in legislatures of India.

key_points: Reservation of at least one-third seats for women in Parliament and State Legislatures through a constitutional amendment.
Political parties should voluntarily give more tickets to women candidates and create reserved positions within party structures.

questions.solution: Two measures to increase women's representation in Indian legislatures are as follows. First, constitutional reservation of at least one-third seats for women in Parliament and State Assemblies (as proposed in the Women's Reservation Bill) would ensure guaranteed representation. Second, political parties should voluntarily allocate a higher proportion of election tickets to women candidates and also create reserved positions within party organizations, making it easier for women to enter and rise in politics.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत की विधायिकाओं में महिलाओं का प्रतिनिधित्व बढ़ाने के दो उपाय हैं। पहला, संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं में महिलाओं के लिए कम से कम एक-तिहाई सीटें आरक्षित करने का संवैधानिक प्रावधान। दूसरा, राजनीतिक दलों को स्वेच्छा से अधिक महिला प्रत्याशियों को टिकट देना चाहिए और पार्टी संगठनों में महिलाओं के लिए पद आरक्षित करने चाहिए।

questions.text: (क) भारत में 'आधुनिक राष्ट्रवाद' के उदय में उपनिवेशवाद विरोधी आंदोलन की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए। अथवा (ख) गाँधीजी ने क्यों कहा कि 'सत्याग्रह तो शुद्ध आत्मबल है'? दो तर्क देकर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Explain the role of anti-colonial movement in the rise of 'modern nationalism' in India. OR (b) Why did Gandhiji say 'Satyagraha is pure soul-force'? Explain by giving two arguments.

sub_questions.text: भारत में 'आधुनिक राष्ट्रवाद' के उदय में उपनिवेशवाद विरोधी आंदोलन की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of anti-colonial movement in the rise of 'modern nationalism' in India.

key_points: Anti-colonial movements united people against British rule and created a shared sense of national identity.
Leaders like Gandhi mobilized masses across castes, religions, and regions, fostering a collective 'Indian' identity that became the foundation of modern nationalism.

sub_questions.solution: The anti-colonial movement played a crucial role in the rise of modern nationalism in India. As people from different regions, castes, and religions came together to fight British colonial rule, they developed a shared sense of collective identity as 'Indians.' Leaders like Mahatma Gandhi mobilized the masses through movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement and Civil Disobedience Movement. These movements transcended social divisions, creating a unified national consciousness that became the foundation of modern Indian nationalism.

sub_questions.text: गाँधीजी ने क्यों कहा कि 'सत्याग्रह तो शुद्ध आत्मबल है'? दो तर्क देकर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhiji say 'Satyagraha is pure soul-force'? Explain by giving two arguments.

key_points: Satyagraha relies on the inner strength of truth and non-violence rather than physical force or weapons.
It appealed to the conscience of the oppressor through moral persuasion, not coercion, making it a spiritual and ethical force.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji called Satyagraha 'pure soul-force' for two reasons. First, Satyagraha did not rely on physical weapons or violence; instead, it drew its strength from the inner conviction of truth (Satya) and non-violence (Ahimsa). A true Satyagrahi could win even the most powerful opponent through moral courage alone. Second, it worked by appealing to the conscience and moral sense of the oppressor rather than coercing or intimidating them, making it an ethical and spiritual force, not a physical one.

questions.text: "महात्मा गाँधी के विचारों और स्वराज की अवधारणा के बारे में मज़दूरों की अपनी समझ थी।" असम के बागानी मज़दूरों के संदर्भ में इस कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Workers too had their own understanding of Mahatma Gandhi and the notion of Swaraj." Support the statement in context of plantation workers of Assam.

key_points: Assam plantation workers interpreted Swaraj as the freedom to move freely and return to their villages — freedom from the Inland Emigration Act.
When they heard of the Non-Cooperation Movement, they left plantations without permission, believing Gandhi's Swaraj meant the right to move freely.
This shows workers gave Swaraj a meaning relevant to their own lives — freedom from colonial labor laws — different from the political meaning.

questions.solution: The plantation workers of Assam had their own unique understanding of Gandhi's concept of Swaraj. Under the Inland Emigration Act of 1859, plantation workers in Assam were not allowed to leave the tea gardens without permission from their employers. When they heard about the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-21) and Gandhi's idea of Swaraj, they interpreted it as the freedom to move freely and return to their home villages. Believing that Swaraj had come, thousands of workers left the plantations without permission and began walking home. Many were caught, beaten, and sent back. This episode shows that workers gave Swaraj a meaning deeply connected to their everyday suffering — freedom from oppressive labor laws — rather than merely political independence.
questions.solution_hindi: असम के बागानी मज़दूरों की गाँधी जी के स्वराज की अवधारणा के बारे में अपनी अलग समझ थी। 1859 के आंतरिक प्रवास अधिनियम के अंतर्गत बागानी मज़दूर नियोक्ता की अनुमति के बिना बागान नहीं छोड़ सकते थे। जब उन्होंने असहयोग आंदोलन और स्वराज के बारे में सुना, तो उन्होंने इसे अपने गाँव वापस लौटने की स्वतंत्रता के रूप में समझा। हज़ारों मज़दूर बिना अनुमति बागान छोड़कर घर की ओर चल पड़े। यह प्रसंग दिखाता है कि मज़दूरों ने स्वराज को अपने जीवन की परिस्थितियों के अनुसार परिभाषित किया।

questions.text: (क) लोकतंत्र में राजनीतिक दलों के महत्त्व की व्याख्या कीजिए। अथवा (ख) भारत ने बहुदलीय व्यवस्था को क्यों अपनाया? उचित तर्कों सहित व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Explain the importance of political parties in democracy. OR (b) Why did India adopt the multiparty system? Explain with suitable arguments.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र में राजनीतिक दलों के महत्त्व की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the importance of political parties in democracy.

key_points: Political parties contest elections and form governments, giving citizens a choice of representatives and policies.
They play a role in forming and running governments, making laws in legislatures, and providing opposition to check government.
They shape public opinion, educate citizens on policies, and serve as a link between the government and the people.

sub_questions.solution: Political parties are essential to the functioning of democracy. They contest elections and give voters a choice between different candidates and policies, thus making representative government possible. Parties that win elections form the government and implement policies, while losing parties form the opposition, which checks and critiques the government's actions. Political parties also play a vital role in making legislation in Parliament. They mobilize voters, shape public opinion, and serve as a crucial link between the citizens and the government. Without political parties, democratic governance would be impossible in large modern states.

sub_questions.text: भारत ने बहुदलीय व्यवस्था को क्यों अपनाया? उचित तर्कों सहित व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did India adopt the multiparty system? Explain with suitable arguments.

key_points: India's vast social, cultural, linguistic, and regional diversity requires multiple parties to represent different sections of society.
The large size and federal nature of India makes it difficult for one or two parties to represent all interests.
A multiparty system ensures wider participation, prevents monopoly of power, and reflects India's democratic diversity.

sub_questions.solution: India adopted the multiparty system due to several reasons. First, India is an extremely diverse nation with hundreds of languages, numerous religions, castes, regions, and communities. No single party can represent all these diverse social groups effectively. Second, India's large size and federal structure mean that regional issues and identities are very strong, requiring regional parties to give voice to local aspirations. Third, a multiparty system ensures that power is not concentrated in the hands of one or two parties, thereby strengthening democracy. It allows wider political participation and prevents authoritarianism.

questions.text: "सत्ता की साझेदारी दरअसल लोकतंत्र की आत्मा है।" इस कथन की उपयुक्त तर्क देकर पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy." Support the statement by giving suitable arguments.

key_points: Power sharing prevents concentration of power in one hand, thus avoiding tyranny and protecting rights of all.
It reflects the will of the people by including various groups and communities in governance, making democracy more inclusive.
It reduces conflict between communities as all groups feel represented, leading to stable and peaceful governance.

questions.solution: Power sharing is indeed the very spirit of democracy, for the following reasons. First, it prevents the concentration of power in one institution or individual, thereby reducing the risk of tyranny and protecting the rights of all citizens. Second, it ensures that the government reflects the will of the people by including different social groups, communities, regions, and institutions in the decision-making process, making governance truly inclusive. Third, when different communities share power, conflicts between them are reduced because every group feels it has a voice. This leads to greater social harmony and political stability, which are essential conditions for a functioning democracy.

Read the story of Rinjha and answer the question that follows:

Story of Rinjha

Rinjha lived with her family in a small village at the outskirts of Diphu in Assam. She enjoys watching her family members clearing, slashing and burning a patch of land for cultivation. She often helps them in irrigating the fields with water running through a bamboo canal from the nearby spring. She loves the surroundings and wants to stay here as long as she can, but this little girl has no idea about the declining fertility of the soil and her family's search for a fresh patch of land in the next season.

What type of farming is Rinjha's family doing? Describe any two of its characteristics.

key_points: Rinjha's family is practising Shifting Cultivation (Slash and Burn / Jhum cultivation).
Characteristic 1: A patch of forest is cleared by cutting and burning vegetation (slash and burn method).
Characteristic 2: Once the soil loses its fertility, the family moves to a new patch of land — it is a shifting/migratory form of agriculture.

questions.solution: Rinjha's family is practising Shifting Cultivation, known as Jhum cultivation in northeastern India. It is called so because families shift to a new plot of land once the current one loses its fertility. Two characteristics of this type of farming are as follows. First, it involves clearing a patch of forest by cutting and burning the vegetation (slash and burn method) to prepare the land for cultivation. Second, since the burning of vegetation provides only temporary fertility to the soil, the land quickly becomes infertile, forcing the family to abandon it and move to a new patch of land the following season.

questions.text_english: Explain the difference between organised and unorganised sector of economy with example.

key_points: Organised sector: registered with government, follows fixed working hours, pays minimum wages, provides job security and benefits like PF and ESI — e.g., government employees, factory workers in large firms.
Unorganised sector: not registered, no job security, irregular wages, no social security benefits — e.g., street vendors, domestic workers, small farmers.
Workers in organised sector enjoy better conditions; unorganised sector workers are vulnerable and unprotected.

questions.solution: The organised sector includes enterprises and businesses that are registered with the government and follow rules and regulations. Workers here have fixed working hours, receive minimum wages as per law, and enjoy social security benefits like Provident Fund (PF), gratuity, and paid leave. Examples include government employees and workers in large registered factories. The unorganised sector, on the other hand, consists of small, unregistered enterprises that are not governed by formal regulations. Workers here have no job security, irregular wages, and no social security benefits. Examples include street vendors, domestic workers, casual agricultural labourers, and small-scale craftsmen.
questions.solution_hindi: संगठित क्षेत्रक में सरकार के साथ पंजीकृत प्रतिष्ठान आते हैं। यहाँ कामगारों को निश्चित कार्य-समय, न्यूनतम वेतन, भविष्य निधि, ग्रेच्युटी आदि की सुविधाएं मिलती हैं। उदाहरण: सरकारी कर्मचारी, बड़ी कंपनियों के कर्मचारी। असंगठित क्षेत्रक में छोटे और अपंजीकृत उद्यम आते हैं। यहाँ कामगारों को नौकरी की कोई सुरक्षा नहीं होती और न ही सामाजिक सुरक्षा लाभ। उदाहरण: रेहड़ी-पटरी वाले, घरेलू कामगार।

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the role of Giuseppe Mazzini in the unification of Italy.

key_points: Mazzini founded Young Italy (1831) and Young Europe (1834) to spread nationalist ideology.
He believed Italy must be a unified republic and propagated the idea that God and people together could create a nation.
He organized uprisings in 1831 and 1834 to liberate Italy from foreign rule, though both failed.
His revolutionary ideas inspired future leaders and the Italian masses, creating the ideological foundation for unification.
He was exiled but continued his work from abroad, keeping the spirit of Italian nationalism alive.

sub_questions.solution: Giuseppe Mazzini played a pivotal role in the ideological foundation of Italian unification. Born in 1807, Mazzini was a passionate nationalist who believed that Italy must become a unified democratic republic. In 1831, he founded the revolutionary organization 'Young Italy' to spread nationalist ideas among Italian youth, and in 1834 he established 'Young Europe' to inspire nationalist movements across the continent. He believed that God had intended nations to be the natural units of mankind and that Italians could be free only when they united as one republic. He organised two failed uprisings (1831 and 1834), for which he was repeatedly exiled. However, his revolutionary writings, speeches, and relentless activism inspired future leaders like Cavour and Garibaldi and awakened national consciousness among the Italian people, providing the indispensable ideological groundwork for eventual unification in 1861.

sub_questions.text: "1830 का दशक यूरोप में भारी कठिनाइयों का आगमन माना जाता है।" इस कथन का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "The 1830s were considered the beginning of great difficulties in Europe." Analyse the statement.

key_points: Rapid population growth in Europe led to unemployment and poverty in cities and countryside.
Industrialisation brought cheap machine-made goods, destroying traditional artisan industries and creating large-scale unemployment.
Bad harvests in the 1830s led to widespread hunger, food scarcity, and high prices across Europe.
The 1848 revolutions emerged from this economic distress — workers and peasants rose against the existing order.
Large-scale migration from rural areas to cities added to social tensions and worsened living conditions in urban slums.

sub_questions.solution: The 1830s were indeed considered the beginning of great difficulties in Europe for several interconnected reasons. First, rapid population growth had led to overcrowding in cities and a surplus of labour, resulting in widespread unemployment and poverty. Second, industrialisation, while creating new industries, also destroyed traditional cottage and handicraft industries. Artisans and weavers who could not compete with machine-made goods lost their livelihoods, leading to mass unemployment. Third, bad harvests in the 1830s and 1840s caused severe food shortages and rising prices, pushing the poor to the brink of starvation. Migration from rural areas to overcrowded cities worsened living conditions in urban slums. These cumulative economic hardships laid the groundwork for the revolutionary upheavals of 1848 across Europe, as people rose against their governments demanding better conditions and political rights.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of industries in increasing air pollution and suggest any three measures to reduce air pollution.

key_points: Industries release smoke, dust, fumes, gases (SO2, CO2, NO) from factories and chimneys, increasing air pollution.
Measure 1: Installing filters/scrubbers in factory chimneys to trap pollutants before they enter the atmosphere.
Measure 2: Using cleaner fuels like CNG and promoting renewable energy in industries.
Measure 3: Regulating industrial emissions through strict environmental laws and regular monitoring.

sub_questions.solution: Industries play a major role in increasing air pollution. Factories emit large quantities of smoke, dust, carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and toxic fumes from chimneys during manufacturing processes. The burning of fossil fuels like coal in thermal power plants and heavy industries releases particulate matter and greenhouse gases, seriously degrading air quality. Three measures to reduce air pollution are as follows: First, fitting pollution control devices such as scrubbers and electrostatic precipitators in factory chimneys can trap harmful particles before they are released. Second, industries should shift to cleaner fuels like Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and invest in renewable energy sources. Third, governments should enforce strict environmental laws, set emission standards, and conduct regular monitoring of industrial areas to ensure compliance.

sub_questions.text: जल प्रदूषण बढ़ाने में उद्योगों की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए तथा जल प्रदूषण को कम करने के किन्हीं तीन उपायों को सुझाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of industries in increasing water pollution and suggest any three measures to reduce water pollution.

key_points: Industries discharge untreated effluents containing chemicals, heavy metals, dyes, and organic wastes into rivers and groundwater.
Measure 1: Mandatory treatment of industrial effluents in Effluent Treatment Plants (ETP) before discharge.
Measure 2: Laws prohibiting dumping of industrial waste in water bodies, with strict penalties.
Measure 3: Promoting water recycling and reuse within industries to minimize discharge of polluted water.

sub_questions.solution: Industries contribute significantly to water pollution by discharging untreated or partially treated effluents containing toxic chemicals, heavy metals like mercury and lead, dyes, acids, and organic waste directly into rivers, lakes, and groundwater. This makes water unfit for drinking, irrigation, and aquatic life. Three measures to reduce water pollution are: First, all industries must be required to set up Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs) to treat wastewater before it is discharged into water bodies. Second, strict environmental laws must prohibit the dumping of industrial waste in rivers and groundwater, with heavy penalties for violations. Third, industries should be encouraged to recycle and reuse water within their processes, thereby minimising the total volume of polluted discharge.

sub_questions.text: "हाल के प्रमाण बताते हैं कि देश के कई भागों में भूमिगत जल का अति उपयोग एक गंभीर संकट बनता जा रहा है।" विकास की धारणीयता के संदर्भ में इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Recent evidence suggests that overuse of groundwater is becoming a serious threat in many parts of the country." Evaluate the statement in the context of sustainability of development.

key_points: Sustainable development means using resources to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
Overuse of groundwater depletes an essential non-renewable resource, threatening agriculture, drinking water supply, and ecosystem balance.
Falling water tables in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan show the crisis is real and urgent.
For sustainable development, groundwater extraction must be regulated and rainwater harvesting must be promoted.
Development that destroys natural resources is not truly sustainable and harms future generations.

sub_questions.solution: The overuse of groundwater poses a severe threat to sustainable development. Sustainable development is defined as development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Groundwater is a critical natural resource used for irrigation, drinking, and industrial purposes. In states like Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan, excessive extraction through tube wells has led to rapidly falling water tables, threatening both agriculture and drinking water supplies. If overexploitation continues, future generations will face acute water scarcity. For development to be truly sustainable, groundwater extraction must be regulated through legal limits, and alternative measures like rainwater harvesting, check dams, and efficient irrigation techniques like drip irrigation must be widely adopted to replenish and conserve this vital resource.

sub_questions.text: "विभिन्न श्रेणी के लोगों के विकास के लक्ष्य भिन्न हो सकते हैं।" इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "The development goals of different categories of people may differ." Evaluate the statement.

key_points: Different people have different aspirations: a landless labourer wants more employment, an industrialist wants infrastructure and markets.
Development goals may even conflict — a dam provides electricity to cities but displaces tribals from their homes.
What is development for one group may be destruction for another, showing development is not a single universal goal.
A girl wants freedom and safety; a boy may want higher wages — both are legitimate development goals.
Hence, any notion of development must consider the needs and aspirations of all sections, not just the majority.

sub_questions.solution: The statement that different categories of people may have different development goals is absolutely correct and can be evaluated through various examples. A landless agricultural labourer's development goal is secure employment and fair wages, while a rich farmer's goal may be higher crop prices and better infrastructure. Similarly, a construction of a large dam may represent development for an industrialist seeking electricity and irrigation, but it spells displacement and loss of livelihood for tribal communities living in the submerged area. A young girl's development goal may be access to education and personal safety, whereas a factory owner may prioritize profit and market expansion. These conflicting goals show that development is not a uniform concept. Therefore, any meaningful development policy must take into account the needs of all sections of society, particularly the marginalized and vulnerable.

questions.text_english: (a) Explain any five bases for assessing the outcomes of democracy. OR (b) Explain any five values of democracy.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र के परिणामों का मूल्यांकन करने वाले किन्हीं पाँच आधारों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any five bases for assessing the outcomes of democracy.

key_points: Accountable government: citizens can question leaders and hold them responsible through elections and institutions.
Responsive government: policies are made keeping in mind the needs and interests of all citizens.
Legitimate government: people accept the government as valid because it is elected by them.
Economic development: assess whether democracy delivers growth, reduces poverty, and improves living standards.
Reduction of inequality: whether democracy ensures equal rights and opportunities for all social groups.

sub_questions.solution: The outcomes of democracy can be assessed on five key bases. First, accountable government — in a democracy, rulers are accountable to the citizens. People have the right to question their representatives through elections, media, and public institutions. Second, responsive government — a democratic government is expected to be sensitive to the needs and concerns of all citizens, especially the marginalized. Third, legitimate government — since a democratic government is chosen by the people through free and fair elections, it enjoys legitimacy and public trust. Fourth, economic outcomes — democracy must be assessed on whether it promotes economic development, reduces poverty, and improves the standard of living. Fifth, reduction of inequality — democracy should ensure that political equality translates into social and economic equality by protecting the rights of all groups and reducing discrimination.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र के किन्हीं पाँच मूल्यों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any five values of democracy.

key_points: Liberty: every citizen has the right to free speech, expression, and movement.
Equality: all citizens are equal before the law and have equal voting rights.
Justice: democracy ensures social, economic, and political justice for all.
Fraternity: sense of brotherhood and belonging among citizens regardless of differences.
Dignity: democracy respects the individual dignity of every person and protects rights of minorities.

sub_questions.solution: Democracy is built on five core values. First, Liberty — democracy guarantees every citizen the freedom of speech, expression, movement, and religion. Citizens are free to criticize the government without fear. Second, Equality — in a democracy, all citizens are equal before the law and have an equal right to vote, regardless of caste, religion, gender, or wealth. Third, Justice — democracy strives to provide social, economic, and political justice to all citizens, protecting the weak from exploitation. Fourth, Fraternity — democracy promotes a spirit of brotherhood and social solidarity among citizens of diverse backgrounds, encouraging them to see themselves as part of one nation. Fifth, Human Dignity — democracy respects the inherent dignity of every individual, safeguards minority rights, and ensures that no one is treated as inferior or discriminated against by the state.

sub_questions.text_english: Cooperative societies come under which source of credit?

key_points: Cooperative societies come under the Formal (institutional) source of credit.

sub_questions.solution: Cooperative societies come under the formal (institutional) source of credit. They are registered bodies that operate under government regulations and provide credit to their members at lower interest rates than informal moneylenders.

sub_questions.text: सहकारी समितियों की किन्हीं दो पूँजी के स्रोतों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two sources of capital of cooperative societies.

key_points: Deposits collected from members.
Loans obtained from banks using member deposits as collateral.

sub_questions.solution: The two main sources of capital for cooperative societies are: first, the deposits collected from their own members, and second, large loans obtained from banks by using these member deposits as collateral security.

sub_questions.text: किसानों की आय वृद्धि में सहकारी समितियों की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of cooperative societies in increasing the income of farmers.

key_points: Cooperative societies provide cheap credit for purchasing agricultural inputs, implements, and for cultivation.
They free farmers from the clutches of moneylenders who charge high interest rates, thereby reducing debt burden and increasing net income.

sub_questions.solution: Cooperative societies play a significant role in increasing farmers' income. They provide cheap loans for purchasing agricultural tools, seeds, fertilizers, and for cultivation and trade activities. Since these loans are available at lower interest rates compared to informal moneylenders, farmers save money on interest payments. This frees them from the debt trap of moneylenders and allows them to invest more in their farms, ultimately increasing their agricultural productivity and net income.

प्रिंट और प्रतिबंध

मुद्रित शब्द की ताक़त का अंदाजा अकसर सरकार द्वारा उसको नियंत्रित करने की कोशिशों से मिलता है। भारत में औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन हमेशा तमाम किताबों और पत्र-पत्रिकाओं पर नज़र रखता था तथा प्रेस पर नियंत्रण रखने के लिए बहुत-से कानून पारित करता था। पहले विश्व युद्ध के दौरान, भारतीय रक्षा नियम के तहत, 22 अखबारों को ज़मानत देनी पड़ी थी। इनमें से 18 ने सरकारी आदेश मानने की जगह खुद को बंद कर देना उचित समझा। रॉलट के अधीन कार्यरत षड्यंत्र समिति ने 1919 में विभिन्न अखबारों के खिलाफ जुर्माना आदि कार्रवाइयों को और सख्त बना दिया। द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध की शुरुआत पर, भारतीय रक्षा अधिनियम पारित किया गया, ताकि युद्ध-संबंधी विषयों को सेंसर किया जा सके। भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन से जुड़ी तमाम रपटें इसी के तहत सेंसर होती थीं। अगस्त 1942 में तकरीबन 90 अखबारों का दमन किया गया।

Print and Censorship

The power of the printed word is most often seen in the way governments seek to regulate and suppress print. The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press. During the First World War, under the Defence of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities. Of these, 18 shut down rather than comply with government orders. The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers. At the outbreak of the Second World War, the Defence of India Act was passed, allowing censoring of reports of war-related topics. All reports about the Quit India movement came under its purview. In August 1942, about 90 newspapers were suppressed.

sub_questions.text: 'सेंसर' का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of 'censor'.

key_points: Censor means to officially examine and suppress or prohibit parts of books, newspapers, films, or other material considered objectionable or politically sensitive by the government.

sub_questions.solution: To censor means to officially examine and suppress, remove, or prohibit the publication or broadcast of information — such as news articles, books, or films — that the government considers to be objectionable, politically dangerous, or against state interests.

sub_questions.text: औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन किताबों और पत्र-पत्रिकाओं पर क्यों नज़र रखता था?
sub_questions.text_english: Why did the colonial administration keep an eye on books and newspapers?

key_points: The colonial government feared that nationalist ideas spread through printed media would incite the Indian people to revolt against British rule.

sub_questions.solution: The colonial administration kept a close watch on books and newspapers because it feared the power of the printed word to spread nationalist ideas and incite the Indian people against British rule. Print media had the potential to mobilize public opinion, encourage resistance movements, and undermine colonial authority, which is why the government passed laws to control the press.

sub_questions.text: गाँधीजी ने रॉलट एक्ट के विरुद्ध देशव्यापी सत्याग्रह क्यों शुरू किया? किन्हीं दो कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhiji start a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act? Explain any two reasons.

key_points: The Rowlatt Act (1919) gave the colonial government the power to arrest and detain any Indian without trial, violating basic civil liberties.
Gandhiji believed this act was unjust and undemocratic as it suppressed political activities and denied Indians the right to challenge detention in court.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji launched a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act for two main reasons. First, the Rowlatt Act (1919) gave the colonial government sweeping powers to arrest and imprison any Indian without trial and without the right to appeal. This was a direct attack on civil liberties and the right to freedom, which Gandhiji considered deeply unjust. Second, the Act was passed despite the unanimous opposition of Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council, showing the complete disregard of British authorities for Indian voices and democratic principles. Gandhiji saw it as a black law that needed to be resisted through non-violent mass protest.

ब्राज़ील के शहर पोर्तो एलग्रे ने विकेंद्रीकरण और नागरिकों की सक्रिय भागीदारी वाले लोकतंत्र के मेल का एक विलक्षण प्रयोग किया है। इस शहर के नगर-परिषद के समांतर एक संगठन खड़ा किया गया और अपने शहर के बारे में वास्तविक फैसले करने का अधिकार स्थानीय निवासियों को दिया गया है। इस शहर के करीब 13 लाख लोग अपने शहर का बजट तैयार करने में भागीदारी करते हैं। शहर को अनेक उप-क्षेत्रों में बाँटा गया है — लगभग वैसे ही जिन्हें हम वार्ड कहते हैं। हर उप-क्षेत्र की अपनी-अपनी बैठक होती है जिसका स्वरूप ग्राम सभा की तरह है और इसमें उस इलाके के सभी नागरिक भाग ले सकते हैं। फिर, कुछ बैठकें पूरे शहर को प्रभावित करने वाले मुद्दों पर होती हैं और उसमें शहर का कोई भी नागरिक भाग ले सकता है। इसमें शहर के बजट पर चर्चा होती है। इसके बाद इन प्रस्तावों को नगरपालिका के सामने पेश किया जाता है जो अंतिम फैसला लेती है।

An Experiment in Brazil

A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city has set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city. The nearly 13 lakh people in this city get to participate in making the budget for their own city. The city is divided into many sectors or what we call wards. Each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate. There are some meetings to discuss issues that affect the entire city. Any citizen of the city can participate in those meetings. The budget of the city is discussed in these meetings. The proposals are put to the municipality that takes a final decision about it.

sub_questions.text: 'सहभागी लोकतंत्र' के अर्थ को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of 'participatory democracy'.

key_points: Participatory democracy is a form of democracy where citizens are directly and actively involved in decision-making processes, beyond just voting in elections.

sub_questions.solution: Participatory democracy is a form of democratic governance in which ordinary citizens are directly and actively involved in decision-making processes — such as planning budgets and framing policies — rather than merely electing representatives and leaving all decisions to them.

sub_questions.text: शक्तियों के बँटवारे के संदर्भ में, दिया गया उदाहरण किस प्रकार की शासन प्रणाली को परिभाषित करता है?
sub_questions.text_english: In the context of separation of powers, the given example defines which type of government?

key_points: The example defines a Federal (or Decentralised) system of government where power is shared at multiple levels — city, ward, and municipality.

sub_questions.solution: In the context of separation of powers, the Porto Alegre example defines a Federal or Decentralised system of government, where power is divided and shared among multiple levels — the ward level, the city-wide level, and the municipal council — rather than being concentrated in one central authority.

sub_questions.text: ब्राज़ील के उपर्युक्त उदाहरण से लगभग मिलती-जुलती भारत की व्यवस्था के गठन का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the structure of the system in India which is almost similar to the above example of Brazil.

key_points: The Panchayati Raj system in India is similar to the Porto Alegre experiment.
At the village level, the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat allow local citizens to participate in decisions about local development and budgets.

sub_questions.solution: The system in India that closely resembles the Porto Alegre experiment in Brazil is the Panchayati Raj system (local self-government). At the village level, the Gram Sabha functions like the ward meetings in Porto Alegre — all adult members of the village can participate in discussions about local development, planning, and expenditure. The Gram Panchayat takes decisions based on these deliberations, while higher tiers (Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad) handle block and district-level matters. In urban areas, Ward Sabhas and Municipal Councils serve a similar function, enabling citizens to participate in governance at the local level.
